attacks.their_claim: Esc cancels the running query (when Monaco widgets are closed); the overlay drawer also closes on Esc.
attacks.counter: Two jobs on one key. If the drawer is open while a 40s query runs, does Esc close the drawer or cancel the query? Either answer surprises you half the time, and cancelling during an incident is exactly when you mash keys. Cancel should be Esc Esc (a double press within 400ms) or Ctrl+Break, and the button label should say so. A single Esc keeps the 'dismiss the topmost overlay' meaning.

attacks.their_claim: Export offers 'Re-run uncapped → stream to file' when the result is capped.
attacks.counter: Re-running isn't free. If the capped result came from 'UPDATE ... RETURNING', 'INSERT ... RETURNING', 'SELECT nextval(...)' or a side-effecting function, re-running it executes the write a second time. Offer re-run only for statements the conservative classifier calls read-only, wrap the re-run in BEGIN READ ONLY on every connection color, and label the button with the statement it will re-execute. On amber or red, also show the estimated row count from EXPLAIN (plan only) before streaming 40M rows from prod.

attacks.their_claim: Status bar: connection chip, search_path, PID, tx state, autocommit, staged count, Ln/Col, and on the right selection aggregates (Count/Sum/Avg/Min/Max/Distinct).
attacks.counter: I agree with the bar. I object to the crowding. Selection aggregates and Ln/Col change on every click, and the tx-state pill has to sit at a fixed position in that bar so your eye learns where to find it. Put the identity and tx block in fixed positions on the left that can't be pushed, and the aggregates in a separate right-aligned region that truncates first. Also, 'FAILED in pulsing red' collides with the prod red. Use the error red-orange plus the words 'FAILED — ROLLBACK REQUIRED', and no pulse that runs forever. A permanent animation turns into wallpaper within an hour.

attacks.their_claim: Activity/Locks lives as a rail entry in the 260px sidebar.
attacks.counter: pg_stat_activity with blocking chains, query text, wait_event, xact age and pg_locks modes does not fit in 260px. During an incident you watch it for minutes, sort by xact_start, and cancel or terminate from it. The rail can keep the icon as an entry point, but clicking it should open a full-width Activity tab with 2s refresh (pausable) and a 'blocked by' tree, not a sidebar list.

attacks.their_claim: Opening a table from the schema tree opens a data tab (WHERE/ORDER BY inputs).
attacks.counter: That's great on dev. On prod, a 'browse table' that silently runs 'SELECT * FROM events' plus count(*) on 300M rows starts a sequential scan and can bloat I/O for everyone else. The data tab must use LIMIT pushed into the SQL, never a count(*) by default (show pg_class.reltuples as '~300M est.'), and default ORDER BY to the PK only when it's indexed. It should also show the generated SQL in a one-line footer, so it's clear what actually ran.

concessions: Command registry first (Minimalist and Engineer): one registry feeding the palette, menus, buttons, tooltips and later MCP. This is better than my 'palette as index' framing, because it can also enforce 'when' clauses such as conn.readOnly, which makes it a safety mechanism and not only a discovery mechanism.

Chips instead of a nested result tab strip (Engineer and Minimalist) are acceptable, as long as Messages has a count plus severity color and auto-selects on ERROR, and DML command tags ('UPDATE 3') get their own chips.
Overlay drawer by default, with pin to push, and relayout on transitionend only (Engineer). This is a better default than my 'pinned' bias, and it keeps the grid stable.

Time-boxed per-tab unlock (Minimalist) instead of an inline confirmation on every DML. I drop my 'inline confirm for WHERE-qualified DML on amber' entirely: amber is Jan's daily dev DB, and that friction would train the reflexive Enter I warned about. Typed friction stays only for no-WHERE DML, TRUNCATE, and DROP/ALTER on red.
Prod and no-PK results never enter edit mode in the first place (Engineer). Blocking up front is better than refusing after 40 staged edits.
A statement splitter instead of a parser is fine for finding boundaries, because the gutter bar shows the exact range before execution. My objection is limited to using it for risk classification.

One fixed density with no compact/comfortable toggle, the system UI font, and only a self-hosted monospace (Engineer). These don't affect safety, and a late font swap that changes measured grid widths really would make the grid lie.

The status bar shrinks from 28px to 22-24px (Power User/Minimalist pressure is fair). I'll also drop the diagonal hatch on red. The 2px inset frame is an 'edge', consistent with the Minimalist's 'edges and dots, no fills' rule, and that is enough.

The Engineer's imperative grid budget is compatible with truth-telling: NULL, empty string and whitespace markers are a class toggle plus textContent and need no per-cell components. I support that hill.
rebuttals.revised_hill: Session truth is always on screen, and the server enforces safety rather than the UI pretending to. A non-collapsible strip of 22-24px per editor tab shows the live session, not the configured one: env color, db, current_user (plus the role when it differs from session_user or is a superuser), and a tx pill with words and a timer (AUTOCOMMIT / IN TX 01:12 / FAILED — ROLLBACK REQUIRED), plus the PID and READ ONLY. It refreshes after every statement from a probe: SELECT current_user, session_user, current_setting('search_path'), current_setting('transaction_read_only'), pg_backend_pid(), now() <> statement_timestamp(). If the probe itself fails with 25P02, that proves the transaction is aborted. Where the strip sits is negotiable; that it's always visible and comes from the wire is not. Behind it, locked red sessions run with a session-level READ ONLY default, so even a misclassified 'SELECT purge()' is rejected by Postgres itself.
proposed_compromises: Splitter-as-status-strip (for the Minimalist's row budget): the 22-24px session strip IS the editor/results splitter handle. You drag it to resize and double-click it to maximize, so it costs zero extra rows compared with a plain 4px gutter. When results are collapsed (Ctrl+J) it docks to the bottom. In the calm state it shows only the env chip, db, role and 'AUTOCOMMIT' in muted text. When a tx is open, the role differs, or it's read-only, the relevant pill becomes loud. The chrome stays quiet when the state is safe and gets loud when it isn't, which is the Minimalist's own 'chrome shows live state' principle applied to the most important state.

Power User's Tx Auto|Manual control plus my prod auto-BEGIN: red defaults to Manual. Commit and Rollback buttons appear in the editor's tab-strip action area only while a tx is open, which satisfies the Minimalist (absent when idle) and the Power User (visible to the mouse when it matters). An idle open tx on red gets an amber countdown and auto-rolls back at 60s, configurable. Closing the tab, switching connection or re-running with an open tx or staged edits gets a Commit / Rollback / Cancel prompt.

Friction ladder, final: green = nothing. Amber = nothing, except the staged-edit SQL review that everyone already agreed on. Red locked = server-enforced READ ONLY. Red unlocked (Minimalist's 10-minute per-tab mode, solid 2px red inset frame) = WHERE-qualified DML runs freely inside the auto-BEGIN. No-WHERE DML, TRUNCATE, DROP/ALTER and EXPLAIN ANALYZE of DML need the table name typed. EXPLAIN ANALYZE of non-SELECT always runs in BEGIN…ROLLBACK, and the drawer header says so.

Run/Cancel: one morphing button (Engineer/Minimalist), pinned in the editor tab strip. While running it reads 'Cancel · 3.2s · Esc Esc'. Cancel goes out of band (CancelRequest or a second connection). After 5s still alive, the button offers 'Terminate backend' as a separate, labelled step.

Staged-edit Apply (everyone): drawer review in read-only Monaco, a single transaction, and each statement must report exactly 1 row affected or the whole batch rolls back with the offending statement highlighted. The pending indicator can be the Minimalist's floating bar or the Engineer's header pill, whichever is cheaper. I care about the 1-row invariant, not where the indicator sits.

Messages: a chip with count plus severity color. It auto-selects on ERROR and shows SQLSTATE, message, DETAIL, HINT, CONTEXT and a jump-to-position link that sets a Monaco marker. NOTICEs are captured from Npgsql's Notice event, never shown as toasts.

Activity/Locks: an icon in the Power User's rail or a palette command, opening a full-width tab type (2s refresh, pausable, blocked-by tree, cancel/terminate per row behind a confirm that names the PID and the query). It never opens in the sidebar or the drawer.

History: no permanent pane (Minimalist/Engineer); searchable via palette/Ctrl+H, opening in the drawer. Every entry records connection, role, tx outcome (committed / rolled back / autocommit) and duration. Statements run on red are additionally appended to a local JSONL audit file, about 20 lines of backend code.

Color reservation (everyone already mostly agrees): the saturated prod red appears only as the env signal, and errors and FAILED-tx use a distinct red-orange plus an icon plus words. Token tests check AA contrast for env colors in both themes.

attacks.their_claim: A 32px action strip on every tab, always visible: [Run ▾] [Cancel] [Explain] [Tx: Auto|Manual ▾] [Commit] [Rollback] [Limit 10k ▾], plus connection and database pickers.
attacks.counter: Most of that strip is disabled most of the time. Commit and Rollback are greyed out whenever no transaction is open, which in autocommit mode is always. Cancel duplicates Run, because the two are never usable at the same moment. Limit and Tx mode get set once per connection, not on every query. The strip is 32px of permanent chrome holding about 9 controls, each needing enabled/disabled states, tooltips and focus order, and maintaining all of that costs more than it gives back. The cheaper version keeps what matters to a mouse user. Put one Run/Cancel morph button in the tab strip. Show a tx pill in the status bar only while a transaction is open: 'IN TX 00:42 ▾' opens Commit/Rollback, and it disappears afterwards. Limit and Tx mode become per-connection settings plus palette commands. You get the same visibility with one control that is always meaningful.

attacks.their_claim: Commit = Ctrl+Alt+Enter, Rollback = Ctrl+Alt+Z, Export = Ctrl+Alt+S, pin drawer = Ctrl+Alt+I, density = Ctrl+Alt+=/-.
attacks.counter: On Windows, AltGr is delivered as Ctrl+Alt, and Jan types on a Czech layout where AltGr produces the characters SQL needs (@ { } [ ] \ | # & < > *). Any Ctrl+Alt+letter binding lets typing a character fire a command, or stops the character from reaching Monaco at all; for example, typing `{` while a binding sits on that key. Rollback on the same chord family as a character you type is a real hazard. Rule: no Ctrl+Alt bindings at all, and no browser-reserved keys (Ctrl+W/T/N/Tab). Commit and Rollback go through the tx pill or the palette. If they need shortcuts, use Ctrl+Shift+Enter variants inside the tx context or F-keys.

attacks.their_claim: Table data tabs with separate WHERE and ORDER BY inputs that have 'Monaco-lite autocomplete', plus Compact/Comfortable density toggles (20/22/26px).
attacks.counter: 'Monaco-lite' doesn't exist. Those inputs are either extra Monaco instances (heavy, and it breaks the single-instance/model-swap design) or a second, homemade autocomplete engine that never matches the real one. Cheaper and equivalent: a data tab is an ordinary SQL tab whose model holds `SELECT * FROM t WHERE … ORDER BY …`, with the editor collapsed to about 3 lines. Filtering means editing that query with the same Monaco and its full completion, and 'Show SQL' is free because the SQL is already there. A density toggle triples the grid geometry to QA (row height feeds scroll maths, overscan and the pool size) for a value Jan sets once. Pick one row height, 24px.

attacks.their_claim: No status bar ever. The single tab strip merges into a 36px title row next to the window controls, Arc/Zed style.
attacks.counter: Phase one runs in a browser tab: the page has no title row and cannot reach the window controls. In the Photino/WebView2 phase, a merged title row means a frameless window with custom drag regions, hit-testing, snap layouts and min/max/close buttons drawn by us. That's a week of platform work for a cosmetic gain. 'No status bar ever' also leaves no stable home for the one piece of state that prevents damage: am I inside an open transaction on prod. The Run pill and tab colour show connection and running state, but not tx state, role or read-only. A 22px fixed-height bar costs less than one grid row and, unlike your floating bar, never changes the grid's geometry.

attacks.their_claim: The staged-edits bar floats bottom-centre over the grid and exists only while edits are pending.
attacks.counter: It sits over the last visible rows and the horizontal scrollbar exactly while you are editing near the bottom of the viewport. It also adds a second, competing surface for the same state the header pill and the amber cell marks already show. Keep it simple: the amber marks on cells, a '3 changes · Review' pill in the fixed-height result header, and the count in the status bar. Nothing floats over the data surface.

attacks.their_claim: 28px grid rows with a 24px compact setting; dark mode uses elevation steps instead of borders.
attacks.counter: 28px loses about 15% of visible rows against 24px on a 1080p screen, which works against the rows-on-screen argument you make yourself. Adding a compact setting means two geometries to test. Make 24px the only option. Borderless elevation in dark mode means each theme defines structure differently, so every component needs two separately reviewed looks. Keep 1px hairline tokens in both themes and let the token values differ; one structure, two palettes.

attacks.their_claim: The backend parses every statement and classifies its risk (UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, TRUNCATE, DROP, ALTER) to scale friction, and Run shows a progress shimmer on the running tab.
attacks.counter: Reliable classification needs a real Postgres parser (libpg_query bindings, native binaries per platform). CTEs (`WITH x AS (DELETE … RETURNING …) SELECT`), DO blocks and functions with side effects (`SELECT purge_all()`) defeat anything cheaper, so the guard gives false confidence on exactly the cases that matter. The mechanism that actually saves you needs no parser. On red connections, every non-read-only run executes inside an implicit BEGIN. The result shows 'N rows affected · Commit / Rollback', and the idle auto-rollback timer applies. The typed-name confirmation applies only to the cheap, unambiguous lexical cases: the first keyword is TRUNCATE or DROP, or the splitter sees UPDATE/DELETE with no WHERE token. The shimmer repaints every frame next to the grid; a static elapsed timer gives the same information.

attacks.their_claim: The status bar re-reads current_user, search_path and similar values with SHOW after every statement and shows host:port/dbname, role, search_path, tx state, PID, server version and read-only, never collapsible.
attacks.counter: A SHOW round trip after every statement doubles latency on every fast query, and fast queries are most queries. Most of those values can only change after SET, RESET or SET ROLE, or a function that calls set_config. Read tx state from the protocol, or track it in our session wrapper where Npgsql doesn't expose it, and re-read role and search_path only after statements whose first keyword is SET/RESET or after a failure. Also, nine fields in a 28px bar overflow at any normal width. Keep the high-signal items visible as text pills (conn, user if it differs from the configured one, tx state with timer, READ ONLY). PID, server version and host:port go in the conn chip's tooltip and in the palette ('session info').

concessions: Power User and DBA are right that transaction state had no home in my opening, and that's a real gap. A fixed 22px status bar is cheap and safe for the grid because its height never changes. Moving timings, row count and tx state there also fixes the result-header overflow problem I raised myself. I drop 'no permanent chrome'.
DBA: every PK-based edit must check affected rows == 1 per statement, and roll back the whole batch otherwise. It costs about 5 lines in the C# apply path and catches concurrent deletes and fake PKs.
DBA: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of anything that isn't a plain SELECT always runs inside BEGIN … ROLLBACK, with that stated in the drawer header. It's trivial and it prevents a classic accident.
DBA: Activity/Locks should be a full tab type with a pausable 2s refresh, not a drawer view. It reuses the grid and the tab model, so it costs nothing extra.
DBA: Messages must show the full error (SQLSTATE, DETAIL, HINT, CONTEXT) and jump to the position. Npgsql's PostgresException already carries all of it.
Power User and DBA: Esc Esc is a better cancel than a single Esc, which needs Monaco context-key checks. Double-press can't collide with closing suggest or find, so it's cheaper and safer.
Power User and DBA: highlight the statement range with a gutter decoration before running it. One deltaDecorations call, reusing the splitter I already proposed.
Power User: the pinned drawer's cell inspector should follow the grid's active cell live. It's one signal and costs nothing.
Power User: running a new query over pending edits must block with Apply / Discard / Cancel. That is the cheap way to keep staged work from being lost.
Power User: show the column type (int4, jsonb…) as a second line in the header. The header has a fixed height, so the grid geometry is unaffected, and it is high value.
Power User: the export menu must say the result was capped at 10k and offer 'Re-run uncapped → stream to file'. Server streaming is already the plan, so this is honest at low cost.
Power User and Minimalist: 'Copy as IN (…) list' and 'Copy as WHERE clause' are extra entries in the same backend generator as INSERT. Nearly free.
Minimalist: Ctrl+Shift+C as a filtered 'Copy as…' palette reuses the palette component, so it's a good free entry point.
DBA: distinct markers for NULL, empty string and whitespace-only values. They are one class or prefix applied to visible cells at render time and fit inside the grid budget.
rebuttals.revised_hill: The results grid remains a hand-written imperative renderer outside Angular change detection: fixed 24px rows, a recycled DOM pool, scroll writes only textContent and transform, 60fps on 10k × 40. I'm extending the hill to the grid's surroundings: every piece of chrome around the grid has a fixed height and never appears or disappears in a way that moves the grid. That means a fixed 30px result header, a fixed two-line column header, a fixed 22px status bar, and a drawer that overlays the grid, or pushes it with a single relayout on transitionend. Ideas that would reflow the grid during interaction (floating bars, density toggles, variable-height rows, an animated push drawer, per-cell components) are out. Rich content goes to the drawer.
proposed_compromises: Status bar: 22px, app-level, not collapsible. Left to right: conn chip (env colour, name; tooltip carries host:port/db, PID, server version) · user/role only when it differs from the configured one · tx pill with words ('AUTOCOMMIT' / 'IN TX 00:42 ▾' / 'FAILED, ROLLBACK REQUIRED') · 'READ ONLY' pill · staged-edit count · active result's '1,284 rows · 18 ms'. Right side: selection aggregates (Count/Sum/Min/Max) for the selected range, computed by the backend over the buffered result. Covers the DBA's and Power User's hill without a per-statement SHOW and without a 9-control action strip.

Run/Cancel: one morphing button at the right end of the tab strip ('Run' → 'Cancel 3.2s'). If the backend is still alive after 5s, a second step offers 'Terminate backend'. Commit/Rollback live in the tx pill's menu and only exist while a transaction is open. Tx mode (Auto/Manual) and row limit are per-connection settings plus palette commands. Prod defaults to Manual + READ ONLY.

Prod safety without a SQL parser: a lexical first-keyword check after the splitter, plus an implicit BEGIN for every non-SELECT run on red, with 'N rows affected · Commit / Rollback' and auto-rollback after idle. The typed table-name confirmation appears only for TRUNCATE/DROP, or UPDATE/DELETE with no WHERE, on red. The Minimalist's per-tab 'Unlock writes' with a 10-minute relock is the way to lift READ ONLY.

Command registry first, shared by the palette (Ctrl+K), CDK Menu context menus, keybindings and tooltips. Every context-menu item also exists in the palette with its shortcut. This is what all four of us actually agree on.

Shortcut rules: no Ctrl+Alt (AltGr on the Czech layout) and no browser-reserved keys. Ctrl+B sidebar, Ctrl+J drawer, Ctrl+Shift+M maximize results, Ctrl+P go-to-object, Ctrl+H history (opens in the drawer), Esc Esc cancel, Ctrl+S review staged edits, F4 open the referenced FK row (frees Ctrl+B).

Results header: one fixed 30px row that is semantically a tablist. Result chips appear only when there is more than one result ('1 · 1,284', '2 · UPDATE 3'). A Messages chip is always present, with an unread badge that turns amber on NOTICE/WARNING and red on ERROR, and an error auto-selects it. A chip can be pinned so the next run adds a new chip instead of replacing it. No second tab-strip component.

Data tabs are SQL tabs: opening a table creates a tab whose Monaco model is `SELECT * FROM t WHERE … ORDER BY … ` with the editor collapsed to about 3 lines. You filter by editing the real query, using the one Monaco and its real completion.

Sidebar: no 40px activity rail in v1. The top row is the connection switcher, followed by the schema tree for the active tab's connection (a flattened virtual list). History is persistent per connection in the backend (SQLite), with an append-only audit log for red connections, and is surfaced through Ctrl+H/the palette into the drawer. Activity/Locks is a tab type. A rail can come later if a third panel ever earns permanent space.

Looks, settled: 24px grid rows (the median of 22, 24, 26 and 28), one density, a 13px system UI font, one self-hosted monospace font, a zinc palette plus one accent, env colours as edges, a red inset frame on prod, a distinct red-orange for errors so prod red keeps its meaning, 1px hairlines in both themes, and overlay-only motion at 120–150ms, with no shimmer and no glass.
